shared_elements: carved stone slab/monolith standing in an excavation trench
bird or raptor head in profile with a strong curved beak
quadruped-like creature in profile in the upper zone
horizontal band of repeating pattern separating zones
curvilinear scroll/spiral or hatched filler motifs
flat vertical field divided into an upper and lower scene
justification: The most specific correspondence is that each slab carries an animal in profile in its upper part above a horizontal patterned band, with a large hook-beaked bird head dominating the lower field, and both are shown half-buried in situ, which drives much of the immediate resemblance. The biggest difference is the manner of carving: A is deep, plastic, heavily rounded and curvilinear with scrollwork, while B is shallow, flat-topped, angular and organised into strict stacked registers of small repeated figures, so the hands look unrelated.
